transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood CS), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena, Mark (CTO), Priya (DevOps), Samir (Product)
---
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, im joined by Maya and Ethan, we're the customer success and solutions team who'll help Northstar with onboarding. how's everyone doing?
00:07 Dr. Lena: Doing well, thanks. excited to get this moving. we've been looking forward to understanding the setup and pilot plan.
00:13 Mark: Yeah quick intro from our side, im Mark Reynolds, CTO, priya is our platform engineer, lena heads the data team and samir is product. timeline: we'd like a pilot by end of year if possible, but open to realistic schedule.
00:25 Jordan: Great - that aligns with what we saw in the kick form. Maya, do you want to run through the high level onboarding flow?
00:30 Maya: Sure, i'll keep it high-level first. typical CS kickoff covers: onboarding checklist, security & compliance review, infra/network setup (VPC peering or private deployment), pilot scope and success criteria, and the benchmark runs. then we break into technical deep dive if needed.
00:43 Priya: for us VPC and private connectivity is key, we have strict egress controls and need to use our KMS for key material. also SSO (SAML) integration for user access.
00:53 Ethan: noted. Redwood supports VPC peering and private deployment options; we also have a private control plane for air-gapped installs and KMS integrations. for the pilot typically we run against both hosted and dedicated variants depending on your compliance needs.
01:05 Samir: what's the expected perf difference between hosted and dedicated? that helps product planning.
01:11 Ethan: dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower tail latency under sustained load because you reserve GPU pools. hosted is faster to start and cheaper for very low volume. for typical Northstar workload we'd recommend a small dedicated pool for pilot to hit your SLA - but we can benchmark both.
01:27 Mark: ok. the security pack is important - SOC2, ISO, audit logs, and where logs are stored. we also need to know data retention and deletion policies.
01:36 Maya: i'll share our security pack; it has SOC2 scope, ISO attestations, audit log retention options, and KMS/HSM integration notes. we can also provide an architecture doc for VPC peering and private deployments.
01:45 Dr. Lena: also curious about prompt caching and cost controls - we've been burned by token costs in prior infra.
01:51 Ethan: Redwood Optimize has batching, prefix/KV caching and quantization recommendations. we can configure automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts and suggest quantization profiles to reduce GPU memory and cost. we'll review your sample prompts to recommend settings.
02:05 Priya: network ports and routing - what does peering require? do you use specific subnets?
02:10 Ethan: we'll provide a network checklist but typical requirements: a peering connection or VPN, specific CIDR ranges for the control plane, and rules for NAT/egress if using hosted. for private deployments we hand off less egress but require internal DNS. i'll send the detailed network workbook.
02:22 Jordan: quick question on identity: for admin roles we support SAML single-sign-on and fine-grained RBAC. are you planning to use SSO for the team?
02:29 Mark: yes SSO is required for ops, and we need RBAC so only specific folks can kick off rollouts or change models.
02:35 Maya: that's supported - we can map SAML groups to Redwood roles; we'll include the SSO integration guide in the pack.
02:42 Samir: any constraints around data residency? some clients need EU-only.
02:46 Jordan: we have region controls and private deployments or Dedicated in specific cloud regions can meet residency requirements; we'll flag region options in the pricing doc.
02:53 Dr. Lena: let's talk about success criteria: for us it's 95th percentile latency under 500ms for common prompts, and overall cost per convo under $0.02 after optimizations. can Redwood help set monitoring for that?
03:06 Maya: yes - Redwood Console provides per-route latency and cost breakdowns. we can attach evals and alerting per prompt set so you see regressions. we'll onboard your prompts into our eval harness for continuous monitoring.
03:20 Priya: regarding pilot infra - do you need access to our cloud account for dedicated? we prefer minimal access.
03:25 Ethan: for Dedicated we typically provision in our managed account and set up peering. for Private we can deploy into your account or on-prem - in that case we need IAM roles and limited access. we do not require full admin creds.
03:37 Mark: what's the expected time to provision a small dedicated pool?
03:40 Jordan: provisioning can be quick with our Dedicated offering - usually 3-7 days once contracts are signed and network is ready. Private deployments take longer depending on on-prem or VPC work.
03:49 Dr. Lena: about benchmarks - Ethan, you'll run them? what's needed from our side?
03:53 Ethan: yes i'll run the initial benchmark. we need a sample prompt set, typical sequence lengths, concurrency targets and any special model choices. if you have preferred open models or a custom model we'll account for that. send them via the secure upload link we'll share.
04:06 Samir: model choices - we were looking at a smaller LLM for RAG and a larger one for complex summarization. can Redwood host multiple model variants and route by policy?
04:15 Ethan: absolutely. Redwood supports multi-model routing and fallback policies - you can route by latency, cost or region. you can also pin users to model versions for rollouts.
04:23 Priya: on the encryption side, we need to use our KMS. can you describe integration?
04:27 Maya: yes we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. for Private deploys you keep full control; for hosted we can integrate KMS for key wrapping and provide options for logs encryption. we will include technical KMS notes.
04:38 Mark: any red flags on compliance? we operate in healthcare and need BAAs, PHI handling assurances.
04:44 Maya: we have enterprise agreements and can sign BAA; we'll loop legal on the necessary docs. also our audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
04:52 Jordan: quick recap on timeline: we'll send onboarding checklist + security pack and pricing by 12/09; customer to provide prompts and network contacts by 12/14; SE benchmark by 12/17; pilot kickoff w/c 12/20. sound good?
05:05 Dr. Lena: yes that works.
05:07 Priya: good, i'll start collecting the network info.
05:10 Samir: one last technical - do you have an SDK for event streaming of inference logs? we want to stream outputs to our analytics pipeline.
05:18 Ethan: yes we have webhooks and streaming endpoints and an SDK. we can demonstrate this in the deep-dive.
05:23 Jordan: ok let's open to detailed questions - any outstanding items?
05:27 Mark: pricing curiosity - are there committed discounts for Dedicated?
05:30 Jordan: yes reserved capacity contracts have monthly/annual commits and volume discounts; we'll include a few commit tiers in the pricing sheet.
05:36 Dr. Lena: regarding quality monitoring, can you alert on regression vs a baseline prompt set?
05:40 Maya: yes we tie evaluations to prompt sets and can alert on metric drift; we'll help define the baseline for the pilot.
05:48 Priya: the network workbook link would be great.
05:51 Ethan: i'll attach the workbook in the follow-up email and the secure upload link for prompts.
05:56 Jordan: Alright if there are no more questions we'll wrap. thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the items Jordan and Maya mentioned.
05:59 Dr. Lena: thanks all.
06:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional minor transcription errors (proper nouns), speaker turn markers may be approximate. Shared artifacts: onboarding checklist (link: https://redwood.example/onboarding-checklist), security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack), network workbook (link: https://redwood.example/network-workbook), secure prompt upload (link: https://redwood.example/secure-upload).
